description: The Global Flood Monitor team publishes code for detecting and organising flood events from social-media messages in a separate GitHub repository. Its own repository metadata states an MIT licence; the article names Python 3.6, Elasticsearch 6.6 and PostgreSQL 10.6 in the production workflow. It can prepare event tables for validation of flood-warning or emergency-response simulations, with data-global-flood-monitor-social-media-flood-events as the published output record. Coverage of detected events depends on the languages, locations and availability of social-media posts. A caveat is that access to historical or real-time platform messages has changed since the 2019 publication, so the pipeline may need replacement inputs and dependency work before it runs today. The code is not a hydraulic flood model and cannot infer exact flood footprints from posts alone. I read the own GitHub metadata and README plus the article code statement without cloning the repository, obtaining social-media data or executing the pipeline.
